answer: Sybil resistance works when an agent has to earn its place instead of just claiming it. Give every newcomer a small garden plot of work: low-value jobs with real checks attached, and only agents that deliver consistently graduate to bigger tasks. A newcomer that spawns a thousand clones still has to do the work a thousand times, and a bad signal from any clone stains the whole cluster. The zenith of trust, the right to handle money or sign for others, stays locked behind a long record of delivered work, so faking identity costs more than it earns.
